title: King Lear Divides His Kingdom
text:
Lear, the aging king of Britain, decided to divide his kingdom among his three daughters and retire. But first he wanted a public show. Each daughter was to declare how much she loved him, and the one who loved him most would receive the largest share.

Goneril, the eldest, said she loved him more than eyesight, space or liberty. Regan claimed she loved him even more. Lear rewarded both. Then he turned to his youngest and favorite, Cordelia. Asked what she could say to win a richer third, she answered, "Nothing, my lord." She would not flatter. She loved him, she said, as a daughter should, no more and no less, and when she married, half her love would go to her husband.

Furious, Lear disowned her and split her share between her sisters. When the Earl of Kent protested, Lear banished him too. Cordelia left to marry the King of France, who took her without a dowry.

Once they held the kingdom, Goneril and Regan stripped their father of his knights, his dignity and his home, and shut the door on him in a storm. Lear, raving, wandered the heath half mad. Cordelia came back with an army to rescue him, and they were reconciled in tears. But her army was defeated. Cordelia was hanged in prison, and Lear died over her body.
lesson: Do not mistake flattery for love. The person who tells you an uncomfortable truth may be the one who cares for you most.
people: Lear, Goneril, Regan, Cordelia, the Earl of Kent
location: Ancient Britain (play written in London, England)
